Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent

Class ModelQuery<T extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.ModelQuery<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the model class
public final class ModelQuery<T extends Model> extends Object
The entry point of one model class: makes instances and starts EloquentBuilder queries, as Laravel's static calls on a model do.

Each model class declares one as a constant, which also registers the class's constructor so that Model.fresh() and Model.replicate(String...) can make instances without reflection: 


 public static final ModelQuery<User> query = ModelQuery.of(User.class, User::new);

 User user = User.query.on(db).find(1).orElseThrow(...);

Safe to share across threads; on(org.aristonis.diwan.database.query.QueryFactory), using(org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.ConnectionResolver) and withClock(org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.ModelClock) return new entries. The global scope registry is the one mutable part, and every entry of a class shares it.

  • Method Details

    • of

      public static <T extends Model> ModelQuery<T> of(Class<T> type, Supplier<T> constructor)
      Returns the entry of a model class, not bound to any connection, and registers the class's constructor. A class registers once; later calls for it keep the first constructor.

      A model's relations need its entry: relation(name), eager loading and existence queries find the class's checked relation map through the entry registered here, and a relation to a class without one fails. The class's static initialiser registers it, so a relation to a class whose entry no code has touched yet fails the same way.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the model class
      Parameters:
      type - the model class, never null
      constructor - makes a new instance, such as User::new, never null
      Returns:
      the entry, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null

    • preventLazyLoading

      public static void preventLazyLoading(boolean prevent)
      Turns lazy-loading prevention on or off for the whole process, a port of Laravel's Model::preventLazyLoading.

      While on, reading a relation that is not loaded from a model that came in a result of more than one row throws LazyLoadingViolationException before any query runs. Models from single-row results, new models, loaded relations and typed relation queries such as user.posts().get() are never blocked. Only models hydrated while the switch is on are marked, and a marked model is blocked only while it stays on.

      This is a boot-time setting for every entry and every thread, not a per-request one: set it once at start-up (for example in development and tests) rather than toggling it around a call.

      Parameters:
      prevent - whether to prevent lazy loading

    • on

      public ModelQuery<T> on(Connection connection)
      Returns an entry whose models run on the given connection, with the grammar and processor of the factory this entry's models use now: the bound factory, else the one their resolver (or the default resolver) gives. Its main use is inside a transaction, where the callback's connection must carry every statement: 
      
 db.connection().transaction(c -> User.query.on(c).find(1));
      Parameters:
      connection - the connection, never null
      Returns:
      a new entry, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if connection is null
      IllegalStateException - if this entry's models have no factory to take the grammar from

    • addGlobalScope

      public ModelQuery<T> addGlobalScope(Scope scope)
      Adds a global scope under its class name, or under SoftDeletingScope.NAME for the soft-deleting scope. Every query of the model class applies it, and a scope with the same key is replaced in place. The scope is shared by all threads, so it must be stateless or thread safe.
      Parameters:
      scope - the scope, never null
      Returns:
      this entry
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if scope is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if the scope is a lambda, an anonymous class or a synthetic class, which have no stable name; use addGlobalScope(String, Scope)
